Bollgard technology celebrates 30 years of innovation

Where Ag Is: Jay Mahaffey discusses how Bollgard revolutionized cotton production across the Cotton Belt in three decades since its commercialization.

Whitney Shannon,Staff Writer,Farm PressNovember 5, 2026

link

At a Glance

Bollgard celebrates its 30th birthday.

Biogenetics and boll weevil eradication changed cotton production.

Bt genetics continue pressing forward for cotton.

In the late 1980s and early 1990s, cotton production faced a crisis largely caused by tobacco budworm. This insect pest became uncontrollable across the Cotton Belt, and the innovative Bt trait provided a solution. That bioengineered trait would later be known as Bollgard.

Jay Mahaffey was involved with the technology before it even had a name. The Scott Learning Center manager and science fellow at Bayer Crop Science in Scott, Miss., has been an entomologist at the center for 32 years. He began studying Bt traits in graduate school.

Mahaffey said Bollgard technology seemed like science fiction at the time. “It was the idea that genes from bacteria could be expressed to produce protein in plants. That’s what became the Bollgard franchise of products,” he explained.

Jay Mahaffey, entomologist, manager and science fellow at the Scott Learning Center in Scott, Miss., has been involved with Bollgard since his graduate school days, before the technology even had a name. (Photos by Whitney Shannon)

The evolution of Bollgard

Bollgard, a Bayer product, was commercially released in 1996 (by Monsanto at the time). Bt technology has evolved since its inception while continuing to protect cotton from worm pests. Mahaffey emphasized that Bollgard, in addition to boll weevil eradication, helped establish a cotton pest management system never experienced before.

Related:Cotton prices are finally going up

“It allowed changes in varieties and technologies that made a serious positive contribution to our pest management system,” he said.

Before Bt, farmers largely planted conventional upland varieties like Deltapine 50, Deltapine 20, Sure-Grow 125 and Sure-Grow 501 on acres across the southern Cotton Belt.

“The cotton world, in a search for earliness, had started to grow varieties that were determinate and earlier,” Mahaffey said. “Those were influential. They taught us a lot about how to manage cotton. They taught us a lot about what we could or couldn’t do with insect management. Those are varieties that a lot of folks remember.”

Then, cotton varieties shifted from conventional to Bollgard. In 2003, Deltapine 555 BG/RR, known as “triple nickel,” was released, and Mahaffey described it as a “major breakthrough.”

“Everybody remembers ‘triple nickel,’” he said. “We enabled an insect management system that let us exploit season length to the ultimate goal of increased fruit retention, developing a few more nodes that had fruit on them and developing a plant that could support that fruit.”

In 2005, Bollgard II was released, leading to the well-known variety Deltapine 1646 in the class of 2016. Mahaffey described Deltapine 1646 as the most planted variety, covering the “largest percentage of cotton acreage in modern times.”

He said Deltapine continues to advance, evaluating a set of varieties every year in the New Product Evaluator program, which started nearly 20 years ago. Since then, Bollgard 3 has been introduced to the industry along with ThryvOn technology.

Related:Historic cotton gin restoration merges history, modern technology

The sun may set on a cotton field, but it shines on the Bollgard technology that continues to advance the cotton industry.

Mahaffey mentioned two varieties from the 2025 class that he finds most exciting today. Deltapine 2537 BT3XF is a broadly adapted and high-yielding variety in the Midsouth and upper Southeast, while Deltapine 2522NR B3TXF has tolerance to reniform nematode, along with a full technology package that includes Bollgard 3 for worm pests, ThryvOn to combat plant bugs and XtendFlex as a triple-stack herbicide protection.

“We’ve reduced another stressor in the system like reniform nematodes. That particular variety is an example of how all of these disciplines came together, and it all really started, in my view, with Bollgard,” Mahaffey said of Deltapine 2522. “We have a better pest management system to use. It has enabled us to develop less determinate genetics, put those genetics in the marketplace and give people guidance about how to use [plant growth regulators] as good as they can be.”

The next generation of Bollgard, Bollgard 4 HT4 with ThryvOn technology, is expected to launch by 2029.

About the Author

Whitney Shannon

Staff Writer, Farm Press

Raised in a rural town in northeast Arkansas, Whitney Shannon has a passion rooted in agriculture and education. As an Arkansas State University graduate, her career began in 2007, teaching middle school. After four years in the public classroom, she shifted gears to be a dedicated stay-at-home mom for her two beautiful daughters.

In 2019, Whitney took a job with the University of Arkansas Cooperative Extension Service, and her love for agriculture grew even stronger. While there, she served in the cotton agronomy program and gained an appreciation for soil health. She later accepted a promotion to be the Technical and Social Media Writer for Agriculture and Natural Resources, which further channeled her energy to educate others about sustainable crop production.

Whitney joined the Delta Farm Press editorial team in 2022, and she is ambitious to share timely stories and on-farm inspiration. “Our farmers and leaders in the ag industry have stories to tell. We learn from one another,” she said. “If we keep our successes or failures a secret, then we stifle opportunities to impact those around us. I aim to tell the story of agriculture in the Delta.”

Whitney lives amid acres of row crops in Newport, Ark., where she raises her two “farm girls” along with their spunky Sheepadoodle dog.

translationZh:
**Bollgard的演变**

20世纪80年代末和90年代初，棉花生产面临一场主要由烟草芽虫引起的危机。这种害虫在整個棉花带变得无法控制，而创新的Bt性状提供了解决方案。这种生物工程性状后来被称为Bollgard。

Jay Mahaffey在这项技术还没有名字之前就参与其中。他是位于密西西比州斯科特的拜耳作物科学斯科特学习中心经理兼科学研究员，已在该中心担任昆虫学家32年。他在研究生院就开始研究Bt性状。

Mahaffey说，Bollgard技术当时看起来像科幻小说。“当时的想法是，来自细菌的基因可以在植物中表达以产生蛋白质。这就是后来成为Bollgard产品系列的东西，”他解释道。

Bollgard是拜耳的产品，于1996年商业化发布（当时由孟山都公司推出）。Bt技术自诞生以来不断演进，同时继续保护棉花免受虫害。Mahaffey强调，Bollgard加上棉铃象甲根除计划，帮助建立了一个前所未有的棉花害虫管理系统。

“它使得品种和技术的变革成为可能，为我们的害虫管理系统做出了重大的积极贡献，”他说。

在Bt之前，农民在南部棉花带的田地上主要种植常规陆地棉品种，如Deltapine 50、Deltapine 20、Sure-Grow 125和Sure-Grow 501。

“棉花界在追求早熟性的过程中，开始种植有限生长和更早熟的品种，”Mahaffey说。“这些品种很有影响力。它们教会了我们很多关于如何管理棉花的知识。它们教会了我们很多关于我们在害虫管理方面能做什么或不能做什么的知识。这些是很多人记得的品种。”

然后，棉花品种从常规品种转向Bollgard。2003年，Deltapine 555 BG/RR（被称为“三重五”）发布，Mahaffey将其描述为“重大突破”。

“每个人都记得‘三重五’，”他说。“我们实现了一种害虫管理系统，让我们能够最大限度地利用季节长度，最终目标是提高座果率，多发育几个带果的节位，并培育出能够支撑那些果实的植株。”

2005年，Bollgard II发布，导致了2016年品种类别中著名的Deltapine 1646。Mahaffey将Deltapine 1646描述为种植面积最大的品种，覆盖了“现代最大比例的棉花种植面积”。

他说Deltapine继续进步，每年在新产品评估者项目中评估一系列品种，该项目大约20年前启动。此后，Bollgard 3和ThryvOn技术被引入行业。

Mahaffey提到2025年品种类别中他目前最兴奋的两个品种。Deltapine 2537 BT3XF是一个在密西西比河中南部和东南部上部广泛适应且高产的品种，而Deltapine 2522NR B3TXF对肾形线虫具有耐受性，并拥有完整的技术包，包括针对虫害的Bollgard 3、对抗盲蝽的ThryvOn以及作为三重堆叠除草剂保护的XtendFlex。

“我们减少了系统中另一个胁迫因素，比如肾形线虫。那个特定品种是所有这些学科如何结合在一起的例子，而在我看来，这一切真正始于Bollgard，”Mahaffey在谈到Deltapine 2522时说。“我们有了更好的害虫管理系统可以使用。它使我们能够开发少有限生长的遗传特性，将这些遗传特性推向市场，并就如何最好地使用[植物生长调节剂]给人们提供指导。”

下一代Bollgard，即带有ThryvOn技术的Bollgard 4 HT4，预计将于2029年推出。
